findings.finding: Overlearning is defined as continuing to practice a skill after it has been mastered.
findings.quote: Overlearning refers to practicing newly acquired skills beyond the point of initial mastery.

findings.finding: Physical tasks show improved retention when practiced beyond the point of initial mastery.
findings.quote: The amount of overlearning affected retention: more overlearning led to more retention on both types of task.

findings.finding: Unlike cognitive tasks, physical tasks may show performance gains during the time between practice sessions.
findings.quote: Whereas participants overlearning physical tasks increased in ability during the retention interval, participants who overlearned cognitive tasks decreased in recall ability over time.

principle: Practicing a skill beyond the point of initial mastery can improve short-term retention, though its long-term benefits for physical tasks may vary.
for_the_teacher: Encourage students to continue practicing a movement sequence even after they have performed it correctly once.
Incorporate extra repetitions of a physical movement to help solidify the skill for short-term retention.
when_it_does_not_apply: The effects of overlearning tend to be short-lived, and it may be an inefficient method for long-term retention compared to other strategies.
